newsitem.title: USA: Mexico energy secretary eyes Texas power plants.
newsitem.headline: Mexico energy secretary eyes Texas power plants.

text.p: Mexican Secretary of Energy Jesus Reyes Heroles said on Wednesday that he had had talks with Texas officials about the possibility of buying a stake in generating plants here to provide electricity for Mexico.
He said the idea made "economic sense" and that it had been greeted with interest by Texas Gov. George W. Bush and utility executives.

Reyes Heroles, talking with reporters after a speech here, said he had spoken with Bush 10 months ago about "the possibility of making joint ventures where we could actually buy some of the plants here to bring the electricity down to the northern part of Mexico."
Since then, little has happened, but Reyes Heroles said Mexico was still exploring the possibilities.
"It makes a lot of economic sense. We should really think about it carefully and see if there is interest to do something like that," Reyes Heroles said.
He said Texas utilities had built so many power plants that they had excess generating capacity from which they could profit by selling to Mexico.
For Mexico, the proposal would provide a cheap source of electricity. "You can buy here generating assets at lower costs than it costs us to construct new plants," he said.
Reyes Heroles made his comments in the context of the need for greater understanding and cooperation between the U.S. and Mexico energy sectors.

He said the United States' bias against government control of the energy industry in Mexico had hindered what should be a more cooperative relationship. Without that hindrance, there could be more joint energy ventures such as his proposed purchase of Texas generating plants, he said.
"It's hard for the Americans to understand why is it you keep your oil company," he said, referring to state-owned Petroleos de Mexico (Pemex).
"They get discouraged and they say' well, the point is that you are losing opportunities'...I say 'I'm sorry,'" Reyes Heroles said.

"We (all) want an efficient energy sector in North America. Let's work efficiently...it really doesn't matter that the company who does that on the other side (of the border) is a state company," he said.

Reyes Heroles said that under President Ernesto Zedillo, Mexico will not privatize Pemex, which would require amending the national constitution. "The administration of Ernesto Zedillo is not going to change it (the constitution)," he said.
"(Pemex) is something that's in our history. It's rooted in our emotions, and very Mexican," he said.
